title: 10-Day Costa Rica Itinerary (March): Arenal · Monteverde · Manuel Antonio — Dry Season Adventure
description: The ultimate Costa Rica loop during peak dry season — volcanic hot springs in La Fortuna, cloud forest wildlife in Monteverde, and pristine Pacific beaches at Manuel Antonio. Ten days of zip-lining, waterfall chasing, night walks, and tropical relaxation.

days.title: Arrive in San José → La Fortuna
days.description: Arrival day — scenic drive through the Central Valley to volcano country

activities.name: Arrive at SJO & Drive to La Fortuna
activities.description: Pick up your rental car at the airport (book Adobe Car Rental in advance for their free shuttle service). The drive to La Fortuna takes about 3 hours through gorgeous Central Valley scenery — coffee plantations, rolling green hills, and your first glimpse of Arenal Volcano rising in the distance.

activities.name: Hot Springs Welcome
activities.description: Check into your hotel and head straight to one of La Fortuna's famous hot springs to soak away the travel fatigue. Skip the pricey Tabacón and try Ecotermales or Paradise Hot Springs instead — fewer crowds, same volcanic-heated bliss.

days.neighborhoods: La Fortuna · Arenal Volcano National Park
days.title: Arenal Volcano & Waterfalls
days.description: Full adventure day — volcano trails, a 70-meter waterfall, and lava views

activities.name: Arenal Volcano National Park
activities.description: Start early for the best volcano views — March mornings in La Fortuna typically have clear skies before afternoon clouds roll in. Hike the main trail (3.4 km loop) through old lava flows and rainforest. The 1968 eruption trail passes through a surreal landscape of petrified lava rocks overtaken by jungle.

activities.name: La Fortuna Waterfall
activities.description: One of Costa Rica's most iconic waterfalls — a 70-meter cascade plunging into an emerald pool. The hike down is 500 steps (steep but doable), and you can swim in the pool at the base. The climb back up is the real workout.

activities.name: Místico Arenal Hanging Bridges
activities.description: Walk through the rainforest canopy on 16 bridges (6 are hanging bridges up to 98m long). This is one of the best spots for wildlife — look for toucans, howler monkeys, coatis, and snakes. Hire a guide at the entrance for the best wildlife spotting ($35/person guided, or $26 self-guided).

days.title: Adventure Day — Your Choice
days.description: Adrenaline or slow — pick your own adventure around the volcano

activities.name: Option A: White-Water Rafting on Río Pacuare
activities.description: Costa Rica's best rafting river — Class III-IV rapids through a pristine jungle canyon. Full-day trip with lunch included. This is world-class rafting, consistently ranked in the global top 5. You'll be picked up from La Fortuna around 6 AM. Rappel down 4 waterfalls (including a 60m free rappel), then fly across the forest canopy on zip lines. Desafío Adventure Company runs the best combo tour — half-day, high adrenaline.

activities.name: Night Walk at Arenal
activities.description: March's dry weather makes this the perfect time for a guided night walk. The jungle comes alive after dark — red-eyed tree frogs, sleeping toucans, tarantulas, vine snakes, and if you're lucky, a kinkajou. Book through Arenal Natura Ecological Park.

days.title: La Fortuna → Monteverde
days.description: Scenic transfer day with a stunning lake crossing and cloud forest arrival

activities.name: Jeep-Boat-Jeep Transfer to Monteverde
activities.description: The iconic way to get between La Fortuna and Monteverde. A van takes you to Lake Arenal, you cruise across the lake with stunning volcano views, then another van climbs the mountain to Monteverde. Way more scenic than driving (and avoids the brutal unpaved mountain road).

activities.name: Explore Santa Elena Town
activities.description: Arrive in Monteverde and settle into your hotel. Walk around the charming mountain town of Santa Elena — browse artisan shops, visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (founded by Quakers in the 1950s), and enjoy the dramatically cooler temperatures after the lowland heat.

days.neighborhoods: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve · Santa Elena
days.title: Monteverde Cloud Forest
days.description: Misty jungle magic — the most biodiverse forest on the planet

activities.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve — Guided Walk
activities.description: This is THE reason to visit Monteverde. The cloud forest is home to over 2,500 plant species, 400+ bird species, and 100+ mammal species. A guided walk is essential — the dense vegetation makes self-spotting nearly impossible. Your guide will find quetzals, hummingbirds, glass frogs, and sleeping pit vipers.

activities.name: Selvatura Park — Hanging Bridges & Butterfly Garden
activities.description: After the cloud forest, head to Selvatura Park for a different canopy perspective. Walk 3 km of hanging bridges through the treetops, then visit one of Costa Rica's best butterfly gardens. The hummingbird garden is free and mesmerizing — dozens of species feed from handheld feeders.

days.title: Zip-Lining & Nocturnal Wildlife
days.description: Adrenaline above the canopy, then creatures of the night

activities.name: 100% Aventura Park — Longest Zip Line in Latin America
activities.description: Monteverde's most famous adrenaline experience. The Superman cable stretches 1.5 km across a valley — you fly face-down over the cloud forest canopy. The full tour includes 10 cables, a Tarzan swing, and a rappel. This is the zip line that put Costa Rica on the adventure map.

activities.name: Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve
activities.description: Less famous than Monteverde's reserve but equally beautiful and far less crowded. The trails are well-maintained and the observation tower gives panoramic views of the Arenal Volcano on clear days. March afternoons in the cloud forest have a magical mist-and-sun interplay.

activities.name: Guided Night Walk — Frog Pond or Selvatura
activities.description: Monteverde's night walks are legendary. The Frog Pond of Monteverde specializes in amphibians — red-eyed tree frogs, glass frogs, and poison dart frogs are almost guaranteed in March. Alternatively, Selvatura runs excellent general night tours with snake and tarantula sightings.

days.title: Monteverde → Manuel Antonio
days.description: From misty mountains to tropical Pacific coast — beach mode activated

activities.name: Drive to Manuel Antonio
activities.description: Leave Monteverde early for the 4-5 hour drive to Manuel Antonio. The road descends from cloud forest to coastal lowland — dramatic scenery change. Stop in Puntarenas for a quick stretch, or detour through the Carara National Park area for scarlet macaw sightings at the Tárcoles River Bridge.

activities.name: Settle In & Beach Time
activities.description: Check into your hotel and hit Playa Espadilla — the public beach right next to Manuel Antonio National Park. It's a gorgeous stretch of sand with warm Pacific water, perfect for swimming. Watch the sunset with a beer from one of the beachfront bars.

days.title: Manuel Antonio National Park
days.description: Where the rainforest meets the beach — Costa Rica's most iconic park

activities.name: Manuel Antonio National Park — Guided Wildlife Walk
activities.description: Costa Rica's most visited national park for good reason. Hire a guide at the entrance for a 2-3 hour wildlife walk — they carry spotting scopes and know every sloth sleeping spot, every monkey troop's territory. You'll see three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins, squirrel monkeys, iguanas, and dozens of bird species. After the walk, hit Playa Manuel Antonio inside the park — one of the most beautiful beaches in Central America.

activities.name: Beach & Pool Time
activities.description: After a full morning in the park, spend the afternoon decompressing. Swim at Playa Espadilla, lounge by the hotel pool, or grab a frozen cocktail at one of the beachfront bars. March heat in Manuel Antonio hits 90-95°F, so siesta time is real.

days.title: Kayaking, Snorkeling & Farewell Beach Day
days.description: One last adventure — mangroves, marine life, and golden-hour memories

activities.name: Option A: Kayak & Snorkel Tour
activities.description: Paddle through mangrove channels on the Damas Island estuary, spotting caimans, herons, and monkeys from water level. Then snorkel off the coast near Biesanz Beach — clear March waters mean excellent visibility for tropical fish and maybe a sea turtle. Half-day sailing along the coast with stops for snorkeling, a coastal lunch, and open bar. The catamaran tours cruise past secluded beaches and often encounter dolphins. Planet Dolphin and Ocean King run the most popular trips.

activities.name: Biesanz Beach — Hidden Gem
activities.description: Your last afternoon beach in Costa Rica should be a special one. Biesanz Beach is a short hike from the road — a tiny cove with calm turquoise water, great snorkeling right off shore, and far fewer people than Espadilla. Perfect for a final tropical swim.

days.title: Manuel Antonio → San José → Home
days.description: Final drive through coffee country, last-minute shopping, and departure

activities.name: Drive to San José Area
activities.description: Head back to San José for your flight. The drive takes about 3-3.5 hours. If your flight is in the evening, detour through the Central Valley for a quick coffee farm tour — Doka Estate or Hacienda Alsacia (Starbucks' own Costa Rica farm) are both near the airport route.

activities.name: Last-Minute Shopping & Departure
activities.description: Pick up souvenirs at the Mercado Central in San José (authentic and cheap) or at the airport duty-free. Costa Rican coffee (Café Britt or Doka Estate) makes the perfect gift. Drop off the rental car, grab a final gallo pinto at the airport soda, and head home with a camera full of sloths, volcanoes, and sunsets.

editorialSummary: The ultimate Costa Rica loop during peak dry season — volcanic hot springs in La Fortuna, cloud forest wildlife in Monteverde, and pristine Pacific beaches at Manuel Antonio. Ten days of zip-lining, waterfall chasing, night walks, and tropical relaxation.
